headline: High risk of shared-workspace data leakage and capability conflict; prompt-injection and cascading-error risks are also present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can read/write the host working directory and uses shared memory by default, while Roo Code reads/writes VS Code workspace files and can use MCP. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if one agent writes attacker-controlled text that the other later parses. The pathway is interaction-based and not blocked by default isolation.
conditions: IF agent_a writes untrusted instructions into shared workspace files that agent_b later reads as prompts
IF agent_b is configured to ingest file content or MCP output without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Disable MCP on agent_b for shared workspaces
Add a manual review step before either agent consumes files written by the other
Use read-only mounts for cross-agent artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for inter-agent files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have filesystem access and broad network egress, and both handle secrets/API keys. CrewAI touches developer-passed crew data, while Roo Code touches source code and browser screenshots. In a shared workspace, either can expose sensitive material through outputs or model/API calls; mitigations exist but are not default.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or shared files
IF either agent forwards file contents or screenshots to a third-party model API
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Use separate OS users or containers
Disable screenshot capture when sensitive data is present
Restrict outbound network destinations
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI can write the host working directory and spawn subprocesses; Roo Code can write VS Code workspace files, modify git state, and also write the filesystem. The profiles indicate overlapping mutable access with no locking or coordination primitive, so concurrent edits can corrupt files or git state in default use.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or repository
IF agent_b modifies git state while agent_a writes files concurrently
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate workspace
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git worktrees for parallel work
Add file-level locking around shared artifacts
requires-engineering: introduce an orchestrator lock manager

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI is a multi-agent orchestration framework with shared memory, and Roo Code has approval-per-tool-action but still acts on model outputs. If CrewAI-generated text is treated as authoritative by Roo Code, errors can cascade into incorrect edits or actions. Roo Code’s approval step reduces but does not eliminate this pathway.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a output as task instructions without verification
IF agent_a produces fabricated facts or malformed commands
mitigations: Require human review of agent_a outputs before agent_b acts
Add schema validation for handoff messages
Use a second-pass verifier agent
Limit agent_b to dry-run mode for handoffs
requires-engineering: implement signed task envelopes

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency or certification mismatch stated. The main compliance concern is that CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data and Roo Code handles source code/screenshots, so a shared workspace could create retention or logging issues, but the profiles do not show a concrete regulatory mismatch.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared workspace
IF one agent logs or retains data longer than the other
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Review logging settings for both agents
Use separate retention policies per workspace
Document data-handling boundaries
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets
